max_tire.note: Drivingline says a stock Rubicon runs 35x11.50R17 on the factory 17x7.5 wheel. JeepGladiatorForum owners report 33s on stock Sports without rubbing; opinions differ on 35s, which may touch the flares at full flex.
Drivingline's minimum for 37s on a Rubicon; expect some rubbing off-road. Wheel backspacing is critical, and 4.88 or 5.13 gears are recommended.
AEV package offered with the 2024 refresh on Sport, Willys, Mojave and Rubicon. AEV's Rubicon-only Level II package uses 37s.

timeline.change: Revealed November 28 at the Los Angeles Auto Show: JL-based crew-cab pickup, 137.3 in wheelbase, five-foot steel bed, Dana 44 axles
Production starts in Toledo in April. 4,190 Rubicon Launch Editions offered for preorder on April 4 (Jeep 4x4 Day)

First model year: 3.6 Pentastar with 6-speed manual or 8-speed auto; Sport, Sport S, Overland, Rubicon; Max Tow 7,650 lb. Mojave ('Desert Rated') and High Altitude shown at Chicago. Rear driveshaft recall 19V-636 on early builds

3.0 EcoDiesel V6 (260 hp, 442 lb-ft, auto only) on all trims except Mojave; Willys and Willys Sport added; Texas Trail edition. The diesel later drew two high-pressure fuel-pump recalls (22V-767, 23V-263)
Uconnect 4 7.0 standard on base trims; Alpine audio standard on Overland, Mojave and Rubicon
Last EcoDiesel year: 1,000 Rubicon FarOut editions. High Altitude returns
Refresh: seven-slot grille, windshield antenna, 12.3 in Uconnect 5, standard curtain airbags, Mojave X and Rubicon X, rear locker standard on Willys, AEV Upcountry and Level II packages
Six-speed manual dropped. 4xe plug-in hybrid announced, then cancelled in September 2025
Sahara trim added; all trucks 3.6 V6 with 8-speed auto. Steel-wheel recall 26V-456; power-steering pump wiring recall 26V-363 covers 2021–2025

identify.intro: Every Gladiator looks much the same, but the trim decides the axles, gearing, transfer case and lockers. The difference between a Sport and a Rubicon is far more than badges.

items.head: Rubicon
items.body: Rock-Trac transfer case with 4:1 low range, front and rear Tru-Lok lockers, 4.10 gears, electronic sway-bar disconnect, LT285/70R17 tires and wide-track axles (64.4 in). Look for the locker and sway-bar switches on the dash.

items.head: Mojave
items.body: FOX 2.5 in internal-bypass shocks with external reservoirs, FOX hydraulic front jounce bumpers, 'Desert Rated' fender badges, orange tow hooks, 65.0 in track, rear locker that works at speed in 4-High. Command-Trac 2.72:1 low range, not Rock-Trac.

items.head: Max Tow (Sport, Sport S)
items.body: 4.10 gears, wider 64.4 in track and the 7,650 lb rating (8-speed only, 2020 spec). Without it, Sports have 3.73 gears and a 62.9 in track.

items.head: EcoDiesel
items.body: 2021–2023 only, automatic only and never on a Mojave. The 2023 Rubicon FarOut has a 'Diesel 3.0L' hood graphic; 1,000 were built.

items.head: Pre- or post-2024
items.body: 2024-on trucks have a seven-slot grille with narrower slots, no mast antenna (it's in the windshield), the 12.3 in Uconnect 5 screen and standard curtain airbags.

items.head: Rubicon Launch Edition
items.body: 2020 only, 4,190 built (a nod to Toledo's 419 area code), with special badges and wheels and a leather-wrapped dash with red stitching.
